portName: Port of Corfu (New Port, Neo Limani)
seoTitle: Corfu cruise port guide: Old Town bus, taxi, Old Fortress
seoDescription: Corfu cruise ships dock at the New Port, 2–3 km from the Old Town. Bus 16 €1.30 (2026), taxi about €10, walk 30–40 min. Old Fortress €10 (2026). Back by 16:30.
quickAnswer: Corfu is a docking port: ships berth at the New Port and a free port shuttle takes you to the passenger terminal. The Old Town is 2–3 km away: walk 30–40 minutes along the flat seafront road, take city bus 16 (€1.30 Zone A fare since 20 March 2026, more from the driver) or a taxi for about €10. Start back to the port 90 minutes before all-aboard.
intro: Corfu is one of the easiest Greek ports to do on your own. Ships dock, the walk into town is flat, and the Old Town is a UNESCO-listed grid of Venetian lanes, arcades and two fortresses that fills a whole day on foot. It feels more Italian than Cycladic: tall shuttered houses, the arcaded Liston and a large open square, the Spianada, between the town and the Old Fortress. If you want a beach or the island's west coast, green KTEL buses leave from the intercity station near the port, but with a normal call the Old Town, the Old Fortress and Kanoni are enough.

terminals.name: New Port (Neo Limani) cruise berths
terminals.notes: Ships berth along the New Port quays north-west of the Old Town. A free internal port shuttle runs from the ship to the passenger terminal; some berths are a 5–10 minute walk from the terminal.

terminals.name: Passenger terminal
terminals.notes: Shared with ferries. Wi-Fi, ATM, first aid, car hire desks. Taxis queue outside; city buses 16 and 17 stop in the port area.

walkability.detail: Leave the terminal and keep the sea on your left along the waterfront road. It is flat but busy and has little shade. About 2 km brings you to the western edge of the Old Town at the Old Port (Spilia), 30–40 minutes. The Spianada, the Liston and the Old Fortress are another 10–15 minutes across the Old Town.

transportSections.cost: €1.30 Zone A, €1.80 Zone B (fares since 20 March 2026); more if bought from the driver
transportSections.detail: Runs from the port to Spilia at the edge of the Old Town. Line 17 runs from the port to the upper Spianada (Ano Plateia Liston). Line 15 links the port with San Rocco Square and the airport. Have coins for the on-board fare.

transportSections.time: 30–40 min to the Old Town edge
transportSections.detail: Flat seafront route with the sea on your left. Hot in summer; take water.
Taxis wait outside the terminal. The first drivers usually offer island tours; for a short ride, go to the end of the line. Agree the fare before you get in.
Not all ships offer one. The public bus is cheaper and as quick.

transportSections.mode: Green KTEL intercity bus (e.g. A9 Paleokastritsa)
transportSections.detail: Leaves from the intercity bus station on Eptanisou Avenue, near the New Port. Timetables changed on 10 October 2026 and some departures are cancelled at short notice; check ktelkerkyras.gr on the day.

returnTiming.rule: Leave the Old Town by 15:45 for a 17:30 all-aboard, so you are on board by 16:30.
returnTiming.detail: The bus takes about 10 minutes, but you may wait 15 minutes for one, and a taxi can take 15 minutes in traffic. You then need the port shuttle from the terminal to your berth. On foot, allow 40 minutes from the Spianada to the terminal. If you go to Paleokastritsa, take a bus that gets you back to Corfu Town by 15:00, since return trips are infrequent and can be cancelled.
returnTiming.emergencyFallback: Take a taxi from the rank at the Spianada or San Rocco Square; the ride to the port is 10–15 minutes and about €10. Call the ship's port agent (number in the daily programme) if you will be late.

diyVsExcursion.ship: Guided walking tour; price varies by line
diyVsExcursion.diy: €2.60 bus return (Zone A, more from the driver) + €10 fortress (2026)

diyVsExcursion.ship: Coach tour; price varies by line
Part of island tours; price varies by line
diyVsExcursion.diy: City bus from the Spianada (2026 city fares)

excursionAdvice: For the Old Town, a ship tour adds little: it is close, flat and easy to navigate. A ship tour is worth it if you want to see the west coast (Paleokastritsa, Pelekas) and the inland villages in one day, because green bus connections are infrequent and cancellations happen. Do not book a tour sold mainly on the Achilleion palace without checking what is open: the palace interior has been closed for restoration for several years.

steps.what: Port shuttle to the terminal, then bus 16 or walk along the seafront to Spilia.
Walk through the Old Town lanes to the Church of Saint Spyridon.
Cross the Spianada to the Old Fortress (€10) and climb to the lighthouse for the view.
Coffee or ginger beer under the Liston arcades.
Museum of Asian Art in the Palace of St Michael and St George, or the city bus to Kanoni for the view of Mouse Island.
Walk the lanes towards the Old Port and the New Fortress side, buying kumquat sweets on the way.
Bus 16 or taxi back to the port. On board by 16:30, 60 minutes before all-aboard.

sights.name: Old Fortress
sights.why: Venetian fortress on a rocky headland, separated from the town by a sea moat. Climb to the lighthouse for views over the Old Town and the Albanian coast.
sights.tip: Open 08:00–20:00 from April to August, closing earlier in September and October. The top is steep and exposed; go before noon.

sights.name: Spianada and the Liston
sights.why: One of the largest squares in Greece, with a cricket ground, and the French-built arcade of cafés along its western side.
sights.tip: Coffee is cheaper standing at the counter than seated under the arcades.

sights.name: Church of Saint Spyridon
sights.why: The church of the island's patron saint, with a tall red-domed bell tower and the saint's relics.
sights.tip: Cover shoulders and knees. Queues form to see the relics.

sights.name: Museum of Asian Art
sights.why: A large collection of Chinese, Japanese and Indian art in the Palace of St Michael and St George, the former British residence on the Spianada.
sights.tip: Open 08:00–20:00 from April to October. A good indoor option on a hot afternoon.

sights.name: Old Town lanes (Kantounia)
sights.why: Narrow paved lanes between tall Venetian-era houses, with small squares, churches and laundry lines overhead. The area is UNESCO-listed.
sights.tip: Get away from the main shopping streets (N. Theotoki and Agiou Spyridonos) for quieter lanes.

sights.name: Kanoni and Mouse Island
sights.why: Viewpoint over Vlacherna Monastery on its causeway and Pontikonisi (Mouse Island), with planes landing just overhead.
sights.tip: City bus line 2 leaves from the lower Spianada next to the Liston.

sights.name: New Fortress
sights.why: The larger Venetian fortress above the Old Port, with tunnels and views over the harbour.
sights.tip: Close to the bus 16 stop at Spilia, so it can be your first or last stop.

beaches.name: Paleokastritsa
beaches.howToGetThere: Green KTEL bus A9 from the intercity station
beaches.note: Coves with clear water and a monastery on the headland. Only for a long call; check return times and cancellations.

beaches.name: Mon Repos beach
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk south from the Spianada along the seafront
beaches.note: Small pebble beach by the Mon Repos estate. The closest proper beach to the Old Town.

beaches.name: Faliraki
beaches.howToGetThere: Walk from the Spianada to the waterfront below the Palace of St Michael and St George
beaches.note: A swimming platform and café rather than a beach, with views of the Old Fortress.

commonMistakes.mistake: Paying for a ship shuttle or tour just to reach the Old Town
commonMistakes.fix: Walk 30–40 minutes on the flat seafront or take bus 16 for €1.30 (Zone A since 20 March 2026; more from the driver).

commonMistakes.mistake: Planning a day around the Achilleion palace
commonMistakes.fix: The palace interior has been closed for restoration for about five years; a new works contract was tendered in August 2026. Check what is open before you go.

commonMistakes.mistake: Taking the first taxi in the queue for a short ride
commonMistakes.fix: The front taxis want island tours. Walk to the end of the line for a ride to town and agree the fare.

commonMistakes.mistake: Leaving the fortress climb until the afternoon
commonMistakes.fix: The Old Fortress is exposed and hot. Go in the morning.

commonMistakes.mistake: Assuming the west-coast buses run as timetabled
commonMistakes.fix: Green KTEL departures can be cancelled at short notice. Check ktelkerkyras.gr and build in a buffer.

safety: Corfu Town is safe. Pickpocketing happens in the busy lanes around Saint Spyridon and on crowded buses. Traffic on the seafront road from the port is heavy and pavements are narrow in places. Summer heat is the most common problem on the walk and at the Old Fortress; carry water.
scams: Taxi drivers at the port quoting a high fixed price for the short ride to town. Agree the fare first or use bus 16.
Cafés and restaurants on the Liston adding a cover or service charge you did not expect. Check the menu for charges before sitting down.
Touts outside Old Town restaurants offering a free drink or discount, then a bill with extra items. Choose places that show a printed menu with prices and check the bill.
accessibility: Corfu is one of the more accessible Greek ports: ships dock, there is a port shuttle to the terminal, and the seafront route to the Old Town is flat. Within the Old Town, the Spianada and the Liston are level, but many lanes are narrow and paved with uneven stone. The Old Fortress is steep in its upper parts; the Ministry of Culture has worked to make parts of it accessible, so ask at the entrance. Kanoni can be reached by bus without steps to the viewpoint.
rainyDay: Corfu is greener and wetter than the Aegean islands, and autumn calls can bring heavy showers. The Museum of Asian Art, the Liston arcades and the churches of the Old Town give cover. The Old Fortress is mostly outdoors and slippery when wet.
crowdTips: Several ships can be in on the same day, and the Old Town fills from about 09:30 to 13:00 when coach groups arrive. Saint Spyridon and the main shopping streets are busiest late morning. Go to the Old Fortress at opening and keep the lanes for the afternoon, when groups have moved on. Kanoni is quietest early or late.

faqs.a: No. Cruise ships dock at the New Port, and a free port shuttle takes you to the passenger terminal.

faqs.q: How do I get from Corfu cruise port to the Old Town?
faqs.a: Walk 30–40 minutes along the flat seafront, take city bus 16 to Spilia (about 10 minutes, €1.30 Zone A fare since 20 March 2026, more from the driver) or a taxi for about €10.

faqs.q: Is Corfu Old Town walkable from the cruise port?
faqs.a: Yes. It is about 2.5 km on a flat road. It is hot in summer and has little shade, so take water.

faqs.q: How much is the Old Fortress in Corfu?
faqs.a: €10 full and €5 reduced (2026). Open 08:00–20:00 from April to August, with earlier closing in September and October.

faqs.q: What can I do in Corfu in one day from a cruise ship?
faqs.a: The Old Fortress in the morning, the Liston and Saint Spyridon, lunch in the Old Town, then the Museum of Asian Art or Kanoni and Mouse Island.
Mon Repos beach is a 30-minute walk south of the Spianada. Paleokastritsa on the west coast is about 50 minutes by green bus A9 (€2.80).

faqs.q: Is there a cruise passenger fee in Corfu?
faqs.a: Yes. Greece charges €5 per disembarking passenger from June to September, €3 in April, May and October and €1 from November to March. Your line charges it.
Yes. Watch for pickpockets in crowded lanes and traffic on the road from the port.
